summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with abdominal pain exacerbated by heavy alcohol use. Imaging ruled out gallbladder disease but confirmed cirrhosis and portal hypertension. His pain was attributed to alcoholic gastritis, which improved with proton-pump inhibitor therapy. He exhibited symptoms of alcohol withdrawal, including anxiety and paresthesias, and was treated with IV diazepam. Despite medical advice, he chose to leave the hospital early. Psychiatry confirmed his decisional capacity, and he was discharged on a six-day oral diazepam taper, thiamine, and his usual medications. He demonstrated understanding of the risks and committed to outpatient follow-up.
problems: Alcoholic gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage
